hypotheses.statement: For calibrated ultraweak emitters placed at least 2 mm beneath ex vivo porcine skin, 640–800 nm images will have smaller source-localization error than 400–600 nm images after wavelength-specific detector calibration, whereas the band difference will be absent for surface emitters.

scope.population: Excised porcine-ear skin over calibrated broadband ultraweak chemiluminescent point sources
scope.condition: Sources positioned at depths of 0, 1, 2, and 4 mm with matched emitted photon numbers
scope.comparator: Red/far-red imaging at 640–800 nm versus blue-green imaging at 400–600 nm
scope.outcome: Centroid-localization error, point-spread-function width, and recovered photon fraction at each depth

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: At depths of at least 2 mm, red/far-red localization error is no smaller than blue-green localization error, or any apparent advantage is already present at zero depth.
hypotheses.estimand: The depth-by-band interaction in localization error: [error(blue-green)-error(red/far-red)] at 2–4 mm minus the same difference at 0 mm; the claim requires a positive interaction with a 95% confidence interval excluding zero.

rationale.step: Tissue scattering and absorption can lower the signal-to-noise ratio of in vivo optical images.

Photons below 600 nm are strongly attenuated by scalp and skull, while longer wavelengths are poorly captured by some conventional PMTs, establishing that source spectrum and detector response jointly constrain biological imaging.
Human UPE has been measured from 400 to 700 nm with an LCTF-EMCCD system, so the proposed spectral partition is accessible with current detectors.

For each source, localization error is the Euclidean distance between the known source coordinate and the fitted image centroid; subtracting the zero-depth band difference removes band-dependent camera and lens bias.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Image a NIST-traceable attenuated broadband source or stable chemiluminescent microsource through randomized porcine-skin thicknesses, alternating calibrated bandpass filters and blinded source positions; estimate wavelength-specific transfer functions, centroid error, FWHM, and photon recovery from repeated dark-subtracted frames.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Back-thinned, deep-cooled EMCCD or qCMOS single-photon camera with calibrated 400–600 nm and 640–800 nm bandpass channels and a low-autofluorescence high-NA lens
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This tests the depth-dependent spatial transfer function of tissue rather than merely asserting that scattering reduces UPE signal or that tissue guides photons.

hypotheses.statement: Following a standardized puncture wound in Arabidopsis thaliana leaves, the centroid of red/far-red UPE will move outward from the wound with distance-dependent onset times that track the independently measured ROS-response front, indicating a changing biological source distribution rather than a static scattering halo.

scope.population: Dark-adapted adult Arabidopsis thaliana rosette leaves
scope.condition: Single standardized puncture wound imaged continuously for 120 minutes
scope.comparator: Sham-handled leaves and matched wounded leaves used for independent ROS imaging
scope.outcome: Radial UPE onset time as a function of distance, propagation speed, and concordance with the ROS front

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: UPE remains confined to a stationary wound-centered point-spread function, shows no positive distance-onset slope, or its estimated propagation speed is unrelated to the independently measured ROS front.
hypotheses.estimand: The UPE-front speed from the inverse slope of onset time versus radial distance and its ratio to the independently measured ROS-front speed; the claim requires both a positive distance-onset slope and a speed ratio between 0.5 and 2.0.

rationale.step: Wounding Arabidopsis produces ROS and oxidized biomolecules that can form electronically excited species.
Wounded Arabidopsis shows enhanced UPE and altered spectral kinetics measurable by cryogenic CCD imaging and PMT spectroscopy.
Plant autoluminescence in vivo is concentrated above 640 nm and peaks near 700–750 nm, identifying the highest-yield band for dynamic imaging.

A static optical point-spread function can broaden an image spatially but cannot generate onset times that increase systematically with distance over successive frames; such a slope requires a time-varying source or tissue optical properties.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Acquire one-minute red/far-red UPE frames from wounded and sham leaves; estimate onset independently in concentric and vein-aligned regions after correcting the measured point-spread function. In a separate matched cohort, measure the wound-induced ROS front at the same time points to avoid excitation afterglow contaminating UPE.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Deep-cooled back-thinned EMCCD with a 640–800 nm channel and fast macro lens, plus a visible fluorescence camera for separate-cohort ROS mapping
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: The register links UPE to oxidative chemistry but does not test whether a moving UPE picture reveals the location and velocity of the generating response rather than optical blur.

hypotheses.statement: At equal excess emitted photon numbers, spatially resolved UPE analysis will detect an unknown focal oxidative lesion occupying 5% of an ex vivo porcine-skin field more accurately than spatially summed counts, while summed counts will perform at least as well for a diffuse whole-field perturbation.

scope.condition: Fenton-reagent oxidative perturbations applied either focally to 5% of the field or diffusely over the entire field, with dose adjusted to equalize excess photons
scope.comparator: A spatial generalized-likelihood-ratio detector versus the sum of all pixels from the same camera frames
scope.outcome: Detection AUC at fixed exposure and false-positive rate for focal and diffuse perturbations

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: There is no positive focal-versus-diffuse interaction in the advantage of spatial analysis over summed counts.
hypotheses.estimand: D=[AUC(spatial)-AUC(sum)]focal-[AUC(spatial)-AUC(sum)]diffuse; the claim requires D greater than 0.10 with a bootstrap 95% confidence interval excluding zero.

rationale.step: Fenton-reagent exposure produces a marked two-dimensional UPE response in porcine skin and is associated with oxidative protein modifications.
CCD accumulation time and hardware binning materially determine the quality of two-dimensional UPE images in biological samples.
Using the same raw frames for both analyses holds quantum efficiency, exposure, optics, and total detected photons constant, isolating the information contributed by photon coordinates.
The interaction D distinguishes a genuine benefit of pictures for localized sources from a generic sensitivity difference between camera and counter hardware.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Randomize focal, diffuse, vehicle, and untreated conditions across skin specimens; acquire blinded dark-corrected frames; equalize excess detected counts by titrating dose in pilot specimens; then compare preregistered spatial and summed-count detectors on held-out specimens.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Deep-cooled high-quantum-efficiency EMCCD, 350–800 nm broadband, with selectable 1×1 to 8×8 hardware binning
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This directly quantifies when photon coordinates add discriminative information beyond counting, using identical photon detections rather than comparing unmatched PMT and camera systems.

hypotheses.statement: A focal cortical ultraweak source beneath intact rat scalp and skull will not be localizable to within 5 mm from an external image even in the 640–850 nm band, although the same source will be localizable after scalp-and-skull removal and a superficial scalp source will remain localizable externally.

scope.population: Fresh ex vivo rat heads with intact scalp and skull and matched exposed-cortex preparations
scope.condition: A calibrated UPE-level microsource placed at randomized cortical coordinates beneath the skull
scope.comparator: Intact-head imaging versus exposed-cortex imaging and superficial scalp-source imaging
scope.outcome: Blinded source-localization error, recovered photon fraction, and image contrast-to-noise ratio

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: The cortical source is localized through intact scalp and skull with median error below 5 mm and performance significantly above shuffled-coordinate controls.
hypotheses.estimand: Median intact-head localization error for cortical sources, with exposed-cortex and superficial-source errors as positive controls; the hypothesis is killed if the intact cortical median is below 5 mm and its 95% interval excludes 5 mm.

rationale.step: Two-dimensional UPE imaging has been reported from rat brain in vivo and related to cerebral metabolism and oxidative stress.

Properly dark extracranial measurements indicate that photons below 600 nm are strongly attenuated and that detected head UPE is likely dominated by scalp rather than brain when conventional PMTs are used.
The seed question identifies tissue scattering and absorption as causes of low-SNR in vivo images.
Comparing localization against randomized source coordinates tests whether an apparent hotspot contains source-position information rather than merely excess counts.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Insert a stable, calibrated microsource emitting at biological UPE rates at computer-randomized cortical coordinates in ex vivo rat heads; image sequentially with intact tissues, scalp removed, and skull removed, with separate superficial-source positive controls and blinded coordinate recovery.
hypotheses.required_instrument: NIR-enhanced deep-cooled EMCCD or SPAD camera with 640–850 nm sensitivity, low-f-number lens, calibrated microsource, and light-tight enclosure
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This tests the hidden spatial-identifiability assumption behind transcranial UPE pictures without retesting whether intracranial photon counts correlate with neural activity.

hypotheses.statement: In Papilio protenor during the pharate-to-pupal transition, anterior-to-posterior UPE redistribution features will reduce held-out error in predicting time to ecdysis by at least 20% relative to whole-body photon counts, temperature, and elapsed pharate time alone.

scope.population: Individually staged Papilio protenor larvae entering the pharate stage
scope.condition: Continuous dark-chamber monitoring through larval-pupal ecdysis
scope.comparator: Prediction from whole-body counts, temperature, and elapsed stage time versus the same model plus spatial centroid, anterior/posterior ratio, and hotspot-motion features
scope.outcome: Cross-validated mean absolute error for time-to-ecdysis prediction

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Adding spatial UPE features reduces held-out mean absolute error by less than 20% or increases it.
hypotheses.estimand: Relative error reduction, 1-MAE(spatial model)/MAE(count-only model), evaluated with animal-level nested cross-validation; the claim requires a lower 95% bootstrap bound above 0.20.

rationale.step: Cooled-CCD moving-picture imaging has revealed spatiotemporal UPE dynamics during Papilio protenor metamorphosis, including anterior-localized emission whose source remains uncertain.
Long exposures and binning are established requirements for imaging very low biological photon fluxes.
Animal-level cross-validation prevents adjacent frames from the same insect appearing in both training and test sets.
The relative-error formula directly measures the predictive information in the picture after retaining all count-only covariates in both models.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Record binned one-to-five-minute UPE frames and synchronized thermal images from a preregistered cohort through ecdysis; extract spatial features without using outcome times, and compare nested cross-validated survival or time-to-event models at the animal level.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Deep-cooled scientific CCD or EMCCD with a fast custom lens and 400–800 nm response, plus a synchronized long-wave infrared temperature camera
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This asks whether a UPE movie contains prognostic spatial information unavailable to a photon counter, extending prior descriptive metamorphosis imaging to a falsifiable held-out prediction.

hypotheses.statement: For superficial subcutaneous murine tumors, spatial UPE heterogeneity will predict the histologic viable-tumor fraction out of sample with at least 0.10 greater R-squared than whole-tumor photon counts, tumor volume, and skin temperature alone.

scope.population: Mice bearing superficial subcutaneous AH109A, TE4, or TE9 tumors
scope.condition: Serial spontaneous UPE imaging at one, two, and three weeks after transplantation under controlled dark adaptation
scope.comparator: A baseline model using integrated tumor counts, tumor volume, time point, and skin temperature versus the same model plus preregistered spatial UPE features
scope.outcome: Histologic viable-tumor fraction and its spatial correspondence to the terminal UPE map

hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Spatial UPE features add no more than 0.10 to held-out R-squared for viable-tumor fraction, or their coefficients fail to generalize across animals and cell lines.
hypotheses.estimand: Delta R-squared=R-squared(spatial-plus-baseline)-R-squared(baseline) under animal-level, cell-line-stratified cross-validation; the claim requires delta R-squared of at least 0.10 with a positive bootstrap confidence interval.

rationale.step: Sequential CCD imaging of transplanted murine tumors found UPE related to tumor size and suggested correspondence between UPE intensity and histologic viability.
Modern CCD and EMCCD systems can capture single visible-wavelength photons with quantum efficiency above 90% and image physiological contrasts in mice.
Including integrated counts and volume in both models makes delta R-squared an estimate of information contributed by spatial distribution rather than total brightness or tumor size.
Holding every serial image from an animal in one cross-validation fold prevents longitudinal data leakage.

hypotheses.proposed_experiment: Acquire serial broadband UPE and thermal images under fixed geometry, perform terminal whole-tumor sectioning with blinded viable/necrotic annotation, register histology to the final optical image, and compare preregistered baseline and spatial models using animal-level held-out predictions.
hypotheses.required_instrument: Back-thinned deep-cooled EMCCD with 400–800 nm response and calibrated macro lens, plus a long-wave infrared camera for surface temperature
hypotheses.novelty_self_claim: This converts earlier tumor-count correlations into a direct test of whether image topology adds histologic information beyond intensity, size, and temperature.
